ENVSE 400: An introduction to the application of engineering principles for the promotion of safety for workers, consumers, and the public.
ENVSE 404W: This course explores the principles underlying surface and interfacial phenomena, with emphasis on application to mineral processing and environmental systems.
ENVSE 406: Issues of sampling, analysis, monitoring and control techniques for effective environmental management in the extractive industries.
ENVSE 408: Mobility of contaminants in aquifers; multiphase flow, transport, retardation and attenuation, vapor mobility, aquifer characterization, mathematical models and aquifer remediation.
ENVSE 412: A laboratory study of the principles involved in the characterization and remediation of process wastes with an emphasis on physical separations.
ENVSE 427: The major objective of this course is to teach the design principles for different unit operations commonly employed in environmental pollution control in the mineral, energy, and chemical process industries.
ENVSE 440: Ventilation system design and analysis for control of industrial contaminants; measurements, dilution and local exhaust ventilation strategies; laboratory demonstrations included.
ENVSE 450: Overview of toxicology, epidemiology, exposure assessment, industrial hygiene, environmental laws, and engineering approaches to protecting workers and the environment.
ENVSE 457: Industrial hygiene is the discipline devoted to the anticipation, recognition, evaluation, and control of hazards in the workplace.
ENVSE 470: Quantitative methods of systems analysis, probabilistic risk and reliability analysis, as well cost-benefit, and value of information analysis.
ENVSE 480: ENVSE 480 provides a culminating design experience for students in the Environmental Systems Engineering major.
ENVSE 494: Independent research and/or design projects under the supervision of the Environmental Systems Engineering program.
ENVSE 495: Students work with an advisor to prepare technical memos and a final report summarizing the experiential education gained through employment in inudstry.
ENVSE 496: Creative projects, including research and design,that are supervised on an individual basis and that fall outside the scope of formal courses.
ENVSE 497: Formal courses given infrequently to explore, in depth, a comparatively narrow subject that may be topical or of special interest.
